utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wladimiroff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: May it assist the Court to introduce to you that I am assisted today by Ms. Gillian Higgins, barrister of the bar of England and Wales. She has been appointed by the Registry to assist the amici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we continue with the evidence of the witness, the Chamber sought the original of Exhibit 28 yesterday. I obtained the original, as possessed by the ICTY, of that document from the evidence unit. The arrangement between the evidence unit, the Registry and the Chambers generally is that original exhibits, particularly of documentary, are inspected and returned to the evidence unit because of the problem with the same exhibit being required for different trials. I trust that that will be the position that will obtain here, but in any event, can I now make available for inspection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. We changed the Rules because of the problems we had in an earlier case about that. That was the old practice. The new practice, if you have a look at the Rules, is that the Registry retains the exhibit. Perhaps you'd like to have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. If, having made this exhibit available for inspection, inspection is all that is required, then the exhibit can be returned. If it's required and necessary to be required and retained, then of course it can be retained, but the practical difficulties that were reflected in the earlier practice, and in the general practice of using copy documents, is something that we'd ask you to have in mind. But in any event, here is the original for inspection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you'd like to look at Rule 41. No need to deal with it now, but if you look at Rule 41, you'll see it's plainly the responsibility of the Registry to keep the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm aware of that and indeed I discussed this this morning with the Registry's representative here, but as to this particular exhibit, here is the original, and if I can make it available to the Chamber, the Chamber can then make its decision as to what it wishes particularly to do with this exhibit on this occasion. It might be prudent to ask the witness to look at it first, because it's a document that may itself be a photocopy but has original signatures on it and then that can be explained to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, if the witness sees it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, this is an exhibit that we looked at yesterday in copy form. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The document before you has what appear to be original signatures of yours in blue ink on the bottom of the first page.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The document itself, it's perhaps not easy for me to know, perhaps you can help us. It may be itself a photocopy or it may be an original. Can you help us? Is it itself an original typed document or a written document or is it itself a photocopy?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you explain, then, please, why it has your signature on it in a different colour ink and how you came to have possession of it and so on and hand it to the ICTY investigators.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was found in the place where the police were stationed and the paramilitaries in the village of Frasher i Madh near Mitrovica and, for this reason, I signed it on the bottom to show that this document is mine and was found in the place I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And did you hand that document to the ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I signed this document, I gave this to the investigator who was in Mitrovica and took a statement from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can that now be handed to the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we've seen that. Let the amici see it and also the accused. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There were two other lists that I must deal with. One was a list that the witness referred to which fell in the same category as a list that the Chamber suggested would not be helpful, namely, provision of information by others, so I shan't produce that list although it's now available in translation. The Chamber will recall the witness spoke of the 23 intellectuals, who he dealt with in paragraph 11. There is a list of their names, and I'd ask the witness please to look at the following exhibit which comes in original and translation. If the usher could put the original, or the version in the original language on the overhead projector, please, so that the -- thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We can see in this document that the list of 23 names is contained within a report of some kind. Did you prepare this report yourself?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: When preparing that report, how were you able to give the 23 names that you've listed there?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I talked with -- I talked with witness Xhafer Bajrami, who escaped from this incident, and then I went to the village of Morine in Skenderaj municipality in which, of this family, there are -- there were 12 members of this family, and I talked to them. And I went to Llaushe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, please, by putting the English version on the overhead projector, which covers only the relevant part of the report, and the relevant part of the report, preceding the listing of the 23 names, reads: "On April 19, 1999, at about 8.00 hours in the village of Dreth, municipality of Zubin Potok, 23 Albanians were arrested by the Serb army. Among them was my brother, Zahid Barani, (age 38), my brother-in-law Hasan Dervare (age 40), and ever since, their fate remains unknown."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May that be an exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I turn to the outstanding matters in this witness's summary, starting at paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I want you to help, please, with your knowledge and experience of the KLA in the areas where you were at the relevant times. First of all, in November 1997, at Skenderaj, at a funeral, did you see something of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the 27th but the -- 27th, it was the 28th of November, 1997. I was personally at this funeral where there was Adem Nuraj, chairman of the Council for the Protection of Human Rights and Freedoms in Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And the presence of the KLA there, in what form or what numbers?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statement of Dr. Adem Nuraj, while Halit Geci, the teacher who was killed two days before by Serbian forces, while he was being buried, three soldiers of the KLA appeared, masked, in front of the assembled people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Moving on to February 1998 at Likoshan and Qirez, was there, to your knowledge, presence of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when these murders took place, I'm not aware that there were KLA soldiers in Likoshan and Qirez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And tell us about your own involvement there. Did you attempt to reach those villages?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I tried on the 2nd of March to enter the village of Qirez, but it was no use because it was blockaded by the army and the police and tanks and armoured vehicles of the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Upon your return, what, if anything, did you encounter? Who did you encounter?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the village -- at the wood of the village of Krushevc, near the road, there was a car that had stopped and there were three people in it in the uniforms of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Moving on to September 1998, do the names Jusufi and Ahmet, associated with KLA ...

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both of them were commanders of the KLA in the Shala zone. The first, commander for logistics; and the second was the army commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you have meetings or dealings with them, and if so, what about?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met them, and this was an official visit, an official meeting. The first official meeting with the KLA commander. This happened after the offensive undertaken on 15, 16, and 17 of September 1998, when in the villages of Shala e Bajgores, in Mitrovica municipality, 16 Albanians were killed. Except for one who was elderly, there were elderly women among them. The houses of many villages were partly burned. All their livestock in the fields were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... go into those details because I want to know about your contacts with the KLA at the moment. Your contacts with the KLA was in relation to what and in what effect?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the offensive, I went specifically to look at the situation and to make recordings and take photographs and to take notes from people who had been in these villages. However, unfortunately, no civilian had been among the villages. They had all been forcibly expelled. I met Xhevat Jusufi, logistics commander for the KLA in the village of Bare. I started to receive information from him about the situation and about what had happened and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I suppose you can answer more questions about that if asked. Typically, when there had been attacks on Albanian villages, did you see members of the KLA afterwards?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the army after the offensives, when I went to these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you aware of a KLA presence anywhere close to Mitrovica, particularly in the area of Vaganice?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the question is not clear, and the last question doesn't have anything to do with my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Let's go back to Vaganice, is that a village near to Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Vaganice is the village closest to Mitrovica, about three kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you aware of any KLA presence in that village?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: For what period of time, if you can help us.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September 1998, from the 22nd to the 29th, the army and police and paramilitaries, Serbian forces, undertook an offensive in which 36 Albanians were killed. Fourteen of them were killed with hammers in the village of Vushtrine commune in village of Galice. This is according to witnesses that -- from members of their families. And after the 29th of September, I went through all these villages, and as soon as I entered the village of Vaganice, I came across members of the KLA. And then many times on subsequent occasions, whenever I went to these areas, I met soldiers of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there an occasion in 1998 when you were involved with two European Community observers in negotiations for the release of three Serbs in Polac?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was an occasion, not three Serbs but two Serbs, in the village of Polac in Skenderaj municipality. I went with two EU observers who were stationed in Zhabar, and we went with the intention of securing the release of two Serbs arrested by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were they indeed released?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After three days of talks and a contact with Adem Demaci, the political representative of the KLA, we succeeded in releasing the two Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you aware at this time, 1998, of any KLA members being active in the town of Mitrovica itself?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But as the conflict developed and it maybe deepened, what was your appreciation of the KLA? Was it constant? Did it increase? Did it decrease? Just tell us.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the offensives and the massacres of Albanians at the hands of the Serbian army, police, paramilitaries, and civilians, the ranks of the KLA grew from day-to-day so that people could defend themselves who were faced with extermination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you aware -- first of all just yes or no: Were you aware of incidents where the KLA accepted responsibility for attacks on Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was your source of information about such attacks?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for these attacks, my source was the media in which there were statements in which the KLA accepted responsibility for such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I now turn to NATO bombing. What effect -- I want you to help us about what effect did NATO bombing have? First of all, what effect, if any, did it appear to have on the conduct of the Serbs in relation to Kosovar residents?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the NATO bombing started on the 24th of March, 1999, many parts of Kosovo, especially Drenica, very strict and harsh offensives were undertaken by the Serbian military, police, and paramilitaries where many Albanians were killed irrespective of their age or gender, or sex. If need be, I can mention the case of Izbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, at the moment, generality will do. As to Izbica, were you there yourself or is this something you learned of from others?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About this case, I learned from others, but then I went there and I counted all the corpses, not only in Izbica but in several villages around that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I shan't trouble you for the detail of that at the moment, in any event. Staying with NATO bombing, did you yourself see and hear the bombing?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very often I saw for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In particular, did you see something of bombing at a warehouse of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. About 13 or 14th of April, 1999, I was at a field in the -- in the Vinarc i Poshtem village of Mitrovica, and I saw the NATO planes bombing the depots of the Yugoslav army in the village of Frasher in Mitrovica. The depots were very close to the Bair neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've finished but for one detail I may wish to deal with with this witness. Yes. I wonder if the witness could just -- it's backtracking but it's something I ought to deal with. Exhibit 27, please. And the original is all that I require; I don't require the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we look at number 21 on the list, please. Now, you told us yesterday of this being your name on the list. How do you spell your name, first all, in the Latin alphabet?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name is Halit Barani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Is that with an E or with an A?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With A. The Serbs all the time change the A into E and pronounced my name as Barani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, that's all I ask of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At one point, the Prosecutor yesterday cautioned that if anybody had any objections, they should raise them straightaway. I wish to say first and foremost I object to everything that this witness is saying. And before I move on to my questions, I would like to warn the public that all subsequent questions that we heard from the Prosecutor this morning, including the mentioning of Vaganice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You are not here to warn the public. You are cross-examining this witness. Now, would you kindly ask the first question, please, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I would like to draw your attention to the fact that everything I talked about with my associates over the telephone in the afternoon and during the night, that these are all the things that were mentioned this morning by the Prosecutor in his question. Of course, slightly distorted. Vaganice and his contacts with the KLA and the bombing of Bair, and many other details. And this abuse of my communications by the Prosecutor is something that I believe you are duty-bound to investigate, because he could not have thought of all of this on his own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, have you been listening to these communications?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I, of course, have no access --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I, of course, have no access to the communications of this accused, and if the accused had taken the opportunity to consider the summary that has been served on him for his assistance, he would have found yesterday, before the date of the alleged phone calls, he would have discovered that all the matters touched on in evidence by this witness this morning were dealt with in that summary, served in advance on the accused yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [no interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the Chamber considers what you've said. Counsel is right. The matters you refer to were all foreshadowed in the summary which was served yesterday. Before you make wild allegations of that sort, you should have some sort of evidence for it. Now, can we begin the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Extreme untruths are being mentioned here, so that's why I have to bring up such examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You used to sell tobacco. That was a question, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I sold tobacco in the -- as part of the enterprise Dum of Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During the war, you had a kiosk at the bus station in Mitrovica, right?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, I didn't have a kiosk, and I did not work at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You have Blerim and Xhevdet as your cousins; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they're cousins of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know that they are the main drug dealers in Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know them well because they are cousins of mine, and I don't believe that they do such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about Azem Barani, your relative? Are you aware that he fled to Turkey after having raped a pupil of the secondary medical school?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that Nuhri Barani, another relative of yours, is selling drugs in Germany?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nuhri is a cousin of mine. I know that he is abroad, but I don't know what he does there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you live in the neighbourhood of Tamnik of Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I live in the Ilirida neighbourhood, formerly Tavnik, of Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Tamnik was the centre of the KLA, this entire neighbourhood in Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know how many warehouses of ammunition and weapons of the KLA were discovered in Tamnik, in that same neighbourhood of Tamnik?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of any discovery of this kind, and if you know that, tell us when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This happened prior to the aggression several times, precisely in those events that you describe as the army having attacked innocent civilians, and the army was actually searching these warehouses and discovering ammunition and weapons and even a concealed hospital in this neighbourhood of yours in Tamnik, because the problem is here that every conflict between the army and police with the KLA you treat as an attack of the army and police against Albanian civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness asked me and I answered him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. The first question is this: Was there a concealed KLA hospital in Tavnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Ilirida neighbourhood, formerly Tavnik, there were no hospitals, but there was the state ambulance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The second question was this: It's alleged that you've treated every conflict between the army and police with the KLA as an attack by the army on Albanian civilians. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is not true. It doesn't stand to facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you linked with the killing at the bus station on the day of St. George, that is, the 6th of May 1998, when a policeman was killed, Darko Nikolic, and then Darko Ivaz, another policeman, and then Joca Jovic, also a policeman was wounded? This was a terrorist attack, as you recall. And they link your name to this terrorist attack. What have you had to do with that terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well this case, and it was not a terrorist attack, but the Serb police attacked Jashari in the street after they tried to raid his place, and then he fired in defence and then he was killed. But I have no connection with this killing except for the following day. The following day, I said, I went to the scene of the killing. I photographed the scene. I took notes without knowing who was involved. Later, I understood that the student Hartim Jashari was killed, and I took part in his funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So at the bus station, where two policemen were killed and one policeman was seriously wounded, you claim that it was the police that attacked this terrorist Hartim Jashari.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they tried to -- to raid him, and he happened to be carrying a weapon and fired, and later he was wounded and died of his wounds. It's outside any kind of reason that a person, a single individual, can attack a truck of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you believe that when the police approaches someone at a bus station, asking him to show his ID, that this is an attack and therefore he has the right to kill a policeman; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not happen at the bus station but outside the bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Near the bus station. All right, near the bus station. What is the difference anyway?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference, because it's not at the bus station but it was outside the bus station. If it were to happen in the bus station, that would be different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In what sense would it have been different?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bus station, many Albanians have been searched very often and there has been no single incident like this. But on the night when this incident happened, Hartim, according to the witnesses, was on his own, was alone. He was not accompanied by anyone but he was on his way home. And he knew that if he were to be arrested, he would be gaoled, and in order to escape the situation, he fired his gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And killed three policemen.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this occasion, I know that there was one killed and two injured. This is original -- my original evidence which I got on the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Darko Nikolic and Darko Ivaz were killed and Jom Surjoric [phoen] was wounded. I have already said that. Two were killed, one was wounded. Do you consider this to be a terrorist attack, this -- that Hartim Jashari did?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. He's given his account of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He is the son of Bislim Jashari, who you mentioned, and the cousin of Adem Jashari; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he is not, but the nephew of Bislim Jashari and is a cousin of Adem Jashari. Hartim Jashari was born and brought up in the Ilirida neighbourhood of Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: After this incident, you went to the village of Vrnjica. That is Vaganica, to the KLA base there. That is what you talked about a few minutes ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. This is a lie of the person you have taken the information from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A minute ago you said to the Prosecutor that you were in Vaganice. Now you're saying that it's a lie that you were in Vaganice.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there. But you shouldn't link Vaganice with Jashari. I've been to Vaganice often but not on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am linking the two because I'm asking you whether you fled there because you were involved in this killing. Just give me an answer, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. I can't say yes or no. I need an explanation, because when I took the notes, I went to my office and then I prepared a report, a daily report, which I submitted to the information media and have with me the copy, the original copy of that report. When I say about information, I mean I have daily reports about everything that happened over a period of three years, with the dates, the place where everything happened, and the circumstances in which it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you one of the founders of the KLA in Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true either, because I was not and I am not one of the founders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In Tamnik, you held meetings in the organisation of the OVK at an elementary school called the 25th of May. This is in your neighbourhood. This is close to where you live. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true, and there is no military school in Ilirida, formerly Tavnik. And if the accused knows when that meeting took place, please, I kindly ask him to say that and then I'll say whether that's true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll get on more quickly -- this may take some time, but Mr. Barani, we'll get on more quickly if you just answer the questions shortly and don't argue with the accused. Just answer the questions. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have heard this. Perhaps there is a misinterpretation. The answer is that there is no military school, however, I did not mention any military school. I said elementary school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't matter about the school. He said that he didn't attend any meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In Vaganice, he met the commanders Ismet Hoxha, who is also the murderer of a policeman, of the policeman called Dejan Prica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met many KLA commanders and soldiers, and the case you are referring to, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet with Ismet Hoxha, though?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have met him -- I have seen him often, him and many other KLA soldiers, when I passed through Vaganice village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you did meet with Ismet Hoxha.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I have met many KLA soldiers in every time I left Mitrovica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In Vaganice itself, was Dibrani Jetullah the commander?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Jetullah Dibrani was KLA commander for Vaganice units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet with him often?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times when I passed through, but I don't need to answer the same questions because I already explained that. I told you that every time I left Mitrovica, I met him soldiers and commanders of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There's a picture also with them, a picture of you, a photograph taken of you and them together there in the village.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What kind of photo are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You and, for example, these commanders, Jetullah or somebody else in Vaganice. I'm talking about these photographs when you said that you passed by them.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I have many photographs. But after the war, when we took pictures in various meetings in Mitrovica and outside Mitrovica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There's another commander there, Kurt Jerkin?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an unfamiliar name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend -- or rather, just give a yes or no answer because my claim is that you did attend this. Did you attend a drill by the KLA that was held in the village of Bare as to how Serbian houses should be ransacked and how police stations should be attacked and how terrorist actions should be carried out? So this was a drill, a display in the village of Bare, and you attended it.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. It was not a drill to loot and raid Serbian houses, but it was a celebration of the 28th of November, the day of the Albanian national flag. And I was there to see how things were going. The date was a celebration, and I stayed there for four hours in succession.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So then these KLA units did not display any such thing, did not carry out any such drill?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true. They simply demonstrated their own drill but not the drill that you are speaking here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what is the drill that they presented on that day, on the 28th, the date that you were there? Could you explain this, what kind of a drill this was?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, it was a day of celebration, and there were various kinds of games being played, songs and dances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you said awhile ago that they demonstrated their own drills, not terrorist activities. What kind of demonstration of their own activities was this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Was there any demonstration of KLA activities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there was, on a stage, because it was a culture manifestation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, you said, and I was listening with my own ears, that they were just demonstrating their own drills of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said and I am saying again, I cannot deny that. We don't need to go over this issue again, because it was a drill, I mean, by them performed on stage in honour of the culture performances put up for the 28th of November, the national flag day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. Yesterday in this courtroom, you named several of your neighbours, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I mentioned many names of Serbs but only one name of a neighbour of mine; Momcilo Kokoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I heard you mention several. You stated several first and last names of Serbs who were your neighbours, and you said that they were the perpetrators of some crimes.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names I mentioned, they were never my neighbours. Kokoric was my neighbour. This is what I said. The others have never been my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you knew them. They lived there in your neighbourhood; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Dejan Savic is from Vushtrri by Bula e Vushtrri [phoen], Dragan Juric lived in Zacan [phoen], Zarko Kosovac lived in Dibri [phoen] neighbourhood. Ratko Antonijevic had his house in Ilirida neighbourhood but very far from where I lived because Ilirida has over 10.000 inhabitants, is the largest neighbourhood of the Mitrovica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Tamnik is the largest neighbourhood in Mitrovica, and that is why it was chosen to be the main centre for the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've already dealt with that. Now let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, all the houses of these people were looted and set fire to in Mitrovica, the ones that you mentioned. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true. The houses of my neighbours, none of them is burned. They are intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Those were just the ones that were forcibly taken over. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not taken over forcibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are they empty now, then?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not empty. Albanian families live in them whose houses have been burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And did the owners of these houses let these people live there and occupy their houses?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them, I'm talking about my neighbours, has sold his house, and it was bought by an Albanian neighbour now. The three others, I don't know about what the situation really is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You say you don't know. Very well. You composed lists of Serbs to be liquidated and stuck them up in the library and the Adriatic Hotel. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true. And I don't know who has -- who may have drafted this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you stuck them up on the library building and the Adriatic Hotel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true. In the library, I have an exhibition with photos of massacred Albanians, and I've put them -- next to the photos, I put the names of the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How do you know who the perpetrators are?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I mentioned the names. I don't know what you have heard. You saw the lists yourself. I don't need to go to any further lengths.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned names that you had heard of. Is that sufficient? Is that enough for you to condemn people and stick up their names as the names of killers?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. All the names that I have, I have evidence to prove the guilt, and I am also one of the eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you consider that you have the right to judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's just a comment. He's told you what he did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not, it's a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you consider that you have the right to judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, that's not a proper question. He's told us what he did, and he's told us why he did it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let me move on to my next question then. I'm moving on. It doesn't matter, if you want me to skip over some of these, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know a policeman called Lulezim Ademi? An Albanian,

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Lulezim Ademi very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On two occasions, the KLA shot at him in 1998, intending to kill him. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true that the KLA has shot him. I know of one case, and I can tell you how it happened. It was in a cafeteria where they were drinking, and after a fight, one of them fired a pistol and a local inhabitant was killed from Ura e Gjakut neighbourhood, and he's in prison now for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how do you make the connection between what you've just said and the fact that the father of Lulezim Ademi, the policeman who was shot at, who was a forester, was killed by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? Who was killed by KLA? I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Lulezim Ademi's father, he was a forester, the father.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a forester, but it's not true that he was killed. He's alive and he lives in Dragonica village of Mitrovica municipality. His name is Mehmed, his father Adem, and his last name Ademi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about the brother named Skender, who was abducted? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he's in the list of the people who have disappeared. When I say in the list, I mean the list of the Council for the Protection of Human Rights and Freedoms in Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In what capacity was his name on that list?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the list of the disappeared, as a person whose destiny is not known.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm claiming. You mentioned Shala on several occasions. Now, that area of Shala is the Operative Zone of the KLA which comprises Kosovska Mitrovica, too, and my question is the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ask him if it was, as you suggest, the Operative Zone, as you put it, of the KLA, Shala. Can you help us to that, Mr. Barani? Just a moment. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not clear. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's suggested that Shala was the Operative Zone of the KLA, which comprised Kosovska Mitrovica. Is that right or not, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the Operative Zone of Shala, that is to say, Shala is the Operative Zone of the KLA, and it comprised Kosovska Mitrovica, didn't it? And along the Albanian border. So -- and then we have the Dukadjin Operative Zone along the Albanian border, including Djakovica and Pec. And then furthermore, we have the Pastrik Operative Zone, which is Prizren Orahovac and that particular region. The Drenica Operative Zone is the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you know about any of these others, other Operative Zones as alleged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer and I can tell you what you are interested in regarding the Mitrovica municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. But what do you know about any of the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have heard and -- because it was often -- it came up often in the information media outlets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I don't want to go on enumerating the Operative Zone Lab, which is Pristina, Nerodimlje and so on and so forth, but let's go back to Shala. You went to the Operative Zone of Shala and took pictures of the military exercises in Shala, or monitored.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to your particular neighbourhood, the neighbourhood of Tamnik. In Tamnik in April 1999, when tens of houses were discovered with ammunition storages and the hospital itself, there was fighting in the Tamnik neighbourhood itself. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the ammunition depots, that's not true. Regarding the fighting, in April when the entire population of the neighbourhood was gathered, where all the inhabitants of Mitrovica were, they were driven to Zhabar fields, the males were separated from the females and got on trucks, then some members of the KLA came and started to fire in order to save the parents from -- with their children and the population in general from what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You claim that there was no fighting, that it was the police and army that attacked the innocent civilians. Am I reading you correctly?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please ask me again the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You claim that in April, in Tamnik there was no fighting at all between the army and the police on the one side and the KLA on the other but that what was happening in fact was that there was an attack launched on innocent civilians. Is that what you're saying? Is that what you claim?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm repeating that no fighting took place in the neighbourhood but in the Zhabar fields in lower Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who was the fighting between in Zhabar in Donja Mitrovica? Between whom?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that there was fighting, but when all the population, the Albanian population was gathered there by the Serb police and army in the Zhabar fields, they separated males from females, and the males they put on trucks and then, in some surrounding villages, from some surrounding houses in Zhabar, fire shots were heard. And these fire shots came from some members of the KLA and they aimed to scare the police and to make them withdraw and let the population alone and not massacre them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you're claiming that the KLA shot to frighten the police and the army. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, because nobody was injured or killed. There were no casualties then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And I can tell you that in Tamnik, in that fighting, I have a name, Nejbosa Kocic, a soldier from Belgrade, he lost his life and a large number of soldiers were wounded. Do you happen to be aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that he was killed in Tamnik where you say that nobody did any shooting?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which day do you mean? And then I can reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about April 1999. That was one particular operation when the army and the police took over the warehouses of the ammunition belonging to the KLA, and when it came into conflict with the KLA in Tamnik in April 1999, a number of soldiers were wounded and Nejbosa Kostic, a soldier from Belgrade, was killed in those operations. That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the case on which I was talking about when the population were gathered together, there were no casualties at all. I don't know about other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At Bajgora, the Shala Operative Zone with two brigades had approximately 4.000 KLA fighters. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the numbers of the KLA in any zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you have an idea as to how many there might have been? Because you have submitted a great deal of information. So do you have any idea of how many KLA fighters there were in the Shala Operative Zone, for instance?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were a lot, and I mentioned before that, after the massacres that were committed, those who had weapons - I mean the Albanians - joined the KLA en masse so as to be able to defend their own population from complete extermination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who was it that wanted to exterminate their own population?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Serbian police and paramilitaries and the army who wished to exterminate the Albanian people, who were not the population of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you consider that the population is the same as the KLA? Do you think the two are the same?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA came forth from out of the people so the people could defend -- people could defend their own mothers, fathers, and sisters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many KLA terrorist attacks do you know of, concrete ones that you have knowledge of directly?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "terrorist attacks," I am not clear which attacks you call terrorist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, for example, when three men come and shoot down a whole cafe full of children. I consider that to be a terrorist attack. Or when they shoot at a vehicle belonging to the Red Cross, for example, or a diplomatic vehicle belonging to an observer, or a car belonging to journalists, or when they kill civilians, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Barani, do you know of any attacks of that nature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no awareness of any attacks of this kind, and I can say there were none.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Excellent. You said that the bombing was of no importance at all, and you know full well that, during the war, the centre of Mitrovica was bombed and not only the SUP building but that the mosque was hit in the centre of Mitrovica, too, and that there was a great deal of panic in Mitrovica. For example, when the Mitrovica centre was hit, including the SUP building, including the targeted mosque and everything else, do you consider that this had absolutely no effect on the population? Just give me a yes or no answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think it may be susceptible to a yes or no answer. Let's deal with it in this way: Now, first of all -- first of all -- let's us deal with it. Let us deal with it in this way. First of all, was the centre of Mitrovica bombed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is not true that the centre of Mitrovica was bombed, if we're talking about the city. The military barracks was bombed and also the police station and the arms depots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. So it is alleged that the SUP building was bombed. Was that bombed? Or is that what you call the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was bombed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said the mosque was hit. Was that hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mosque was hit but not by NATO but by the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Dealing simply with NATO. He said that there was a great deal of panic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] People were not scared but were delighted. I'm talking about the Albanian population. Because finally a force had emerged that would save them from extermination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where is the SUP building which you refer to as the police station? Where is it located?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SUP building, which I mean, is in the northeast of Mitrovica, in the Ibri neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So nothing was hit in the centre. Is that it? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two shells fell within the fence of the building of the former Yugoslav army, which is near the market of Mitrovica in the second central neighbourhood. But on this occasion, there was no damage except that the glass in the windows of the buildings roundabout was broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the area of Kosovska Mitrovica, 116 or 117 - I can just be wrong in that one figure - bombs were thrown during the NATO strike, the NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the quantities of bombs that were dropped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it began on the 25th of March, 24th of March. On the 24th of March, two airstrikes. On the 25th, four airstrikes. Do you remember that in Mitrovica, on the 24th and 25th, not to go beyond that, just those two days.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 24th of March, during the night, I heard NATO bombing, but where they fell and how many bombs there were, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You only remember the bombing of the military depot, but that is on Bair hill that you mentioned a moment ago when you were saying that the population was there and was bothered but not by NATO but the Serb forces. That's what you said, is it?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say they were shelled by Serbian forces. I don't say -- and I didn't say that there were people there. I said that I was in a meadow in the village of Vinarc i Poshtem in Mitrovica and somewhere round about the 13th and 14th of April, and there I saw how the depot of the Yugoslav army in the village of Frasher was bombed, and this village is adjacent to the Bair neighbourhood of Mitrovica. That is in my statement. That I saw with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's now 11.00 and time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Barani, we'll adjourn now for half a hour. Could you come back, then, at half past eleven, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Radomir Pantovic?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes and no. Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He worked in the same shop with you in different shifts.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And his relative, Todor Zivkovic, on July 1999, in July 1999, the KLA took him from the cemetery and he was at the cemetery by the grave of his son, and the KLA took him to the building of the social insurance where the KLA headquarters was. Radomir Pantovic, whom you know, who you worked with in different shifts, asked you to intervene so that they would not liquidate his relative. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I have information that he did ask you but that you refused to help him. Let us proceed. You mentioned Fadil Kurti, that he was killed by the Serbs. Fadil Kurti was a policeman. He worked at the MUP. A policeman from the village of Cabra. He worked at the MUP in Zubin Potok; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true, and I didn't mention him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of him?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I've heard this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you do not know about Zumur Aljickaj, his brother-in-law, who called him to come to the village of Llaushe to pick up his wife and then he massacred him there, killed him. You don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of this incident at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In 1996, did you direct a play in which you glorified the killing of a policeman by Adem Jashari?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did indeed direct a play, because I regularly work in the theatre, but this is a very mistaken report. It's not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what was the play? This in 1996, the one related to the killing of the policeman.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the performances were events that happened or could happen, regardless of what these were about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What you have been saying now, is this to say that it has nothing to do with this subject that I'm questioning you about?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- if I'm supposed to explain all the plays that I've directed, there are 53 premiers and ever so many subsequent performances, it would take a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you don't remember this particular play, just say so. If you do remember, just say yes or no whether it was concerned with the killing of a policeman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not -- no performance was about the killing of a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Skender or did you know Skender Ademi?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have known him and I spoke about him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How did he lose his life?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said before; he is counted missing and how he died or whether he died, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I have information that you were directly connected to his kidnapping and that you killed him in the village of Sukovac.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true, and you have extremely erroneous information. This is a pure lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In the neighbourhoods of Tamnik and Bair that we've been mentioning, there were about 100 members of the KLA from Vaganice and Osljani, from the village of Vaganice and the village of Osljani. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've heard anything like this. I haven't said anything of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, you were talking about Tamnik, you were talking about Vaganice. So now I'm asking you whether this group of 100 members of the KLA was in Tamnik and Bair and from Vaganice and Osljani

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think he's answered before that he doesn't know how many members of the KLA there were.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of Ismet Hoxha, Milezim Krasniqi, Fadil Deljic nicknamed Buli [phoen], Avnic Hardimal [phoen], Nexhat Cubreli, Bajram Jaha, all of them being KLA commanders? Do you know of them? Do you know them personally or do you know all of them personally?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know some of them, and they weren't commanders but they were members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And I assert that they were members of the headquarters of that group that was working and operating in Bair and Tamnik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that Bajram Jaha, who was a member of the KLA, as you said, that he was a drug dealer at the same time? You said that his house had been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that his house was burned on 27th of March. And what he was involved in, besides having a restaurant, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. He was a gambler in addition to being a drug dealer and a restaurant owner. Do you know Salj Fehemi, commander of the Intervention Platoon of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I've heard that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am asking you because he was located in Tamnik, and he was in charge of operations in Kosovska Mitrovica, and his house is right by the school called the 25th of May. It's sort of in your neighbourhood. It's impossible for you not to know him. Try to remember. Do you know him or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true that he operated in Tavnik in uniform. It is also untrue that he is my neighbour because I know all my neighbours and people further off, too, but I've never heard this name, and I do not know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know Jakup Ufcu?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that name was said properly, this is the first time that I've heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then I'm not going to put any more questions to you in relation to him. Do you know Feriz Fetah, Pushi Tolla [phoen], the former reserve officer who worked for the security at the Trepca company?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was he also one of the commanders in Shala?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was one of the KLA commanders in the Shala unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know Safet Dobrini, Dobrini Safet? His house is in the neighbourhood of -- called of the 22nd division, near the motel. Do you know about him?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also the first time I've heard this name. And there's no neighbourhood with this name in Mitrovica. I've never heard of such a place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The first time? You don't even know the neighbourhood? The neighbourhood doesn't exist? I have information that this house of his was a collection centre for the KLA in Shala. You don't know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of the existence of any such person or any such neighbourhood in Mitrovica. And I know all the neighbourhoods in Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Have you heard of the following names: Sadik Kurti, Fatik Myftari, Fatmir Serati, Fatmir Serati? Have you heard of these names? Do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Sahid? There are many Sahids and Fatmirs so I don't know who you mean. Just tell me where they live and maybe I can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You have not heard of them as a group or as individuals?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've heard about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you because they were in charge of procuring weapons from Albania and bringing them to Tamnik and Shala. Do you know that when the OSCE mission went, when they left, rather, in the village of Kovacica they left some equipment that the KLA used for monitoring the communications between the MUP and the army?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you know that the monitoring mission, when they left the village of Kovacica, they left some equipment that the KLA used for the monitoring the communications of the police and the army?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know since this communication was monitored with a view to preparing the attack of the entire structure of the KLA against Mitrovica, precisely in order to set the right time for that attack?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know Ymer Myftari from the village of Vllasinje who was a school inspector previously in the municipality of Kosovska Mitrovica and who was later the commander of the KLA in the village of Vllasinje?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Ymer, but I have no knowledge of him being a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was not a big commander. He just had 15 more bandits with him, and they went around killing people.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I don't know anything about this. I know Ymer as an educational inspector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said awhile ago that you did not know anything about clashes between the KLA and the military and the police in Tamnik or of the death of Nejbosa Hodzic, a soldier. Do you know on the 29th of May, 1999, that Ivan Milosevic, another soldier, was killed and that this group that had connections with Mujahedin groups chopped off his head and stabbed him 17 times with a knife in addition to killing him in this way? Do you know of this event?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of anything of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In Bajgora, at this review of KLA troops that you attended, you got a certificate of gratitude. What kind of certificate of gratitude was this?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The certificate is -- was for my office, because I had often visited the villages of Shala after offensives and had attended many funerals of Albanians who had been shot by the Serbian army and police in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were these members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were elderly men and women, including a paralysed elderly woman who was stabbed with a knife in the village of Kacanol in Mitrovica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You are claiming that the army and the police did not shoot at the KLA but at some old men and women. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what always happened during offensives. When I say this, I can say that of the bodies that I saw, not one of them was in uniform; all of them were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You are saying, and also on the basis of everything you've said so far, the Operation Zone Shala, the Operation Zone of the KLA, so far I mentioned so many names and you know at least 15 of their commanders. So this is a large group. You know that this entire structure was fighting the army and the police and was killing people all over, and you claim that you did not see any of them, only old men and women?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I follow the question. What is the question, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the question is how does he explain this - how shall I put this? - highly illogical contradiction between the fact that on the one hand he confirmed here that this Operation Zone of Shala that the KLA covered by covering Mitrovica with a large number of KLA members, and he confirmed himself that he knew at least 15-odd names of their commanders. So this is a big structure. Furthermore, that this entire structure was shooting at the military and the police, fighting against the military and the police. How can he claim that the army and the police were shooting innocent civilians? I'm asking him to explain that. Apart from all these masses of the KLA and these commanders who were commanding someone - and the information we have is that there were 4.000 members - and how can he, in spite of all of that, claim that the army and the military were shooting innocent civilians?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But that is his evidence. He says this is what happened. Now, as I've said before, you can make comments about that, as you've just made, but it's not a question for him. You can ask him, if you like, if he's telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I asked him how does he explain this kind of contradiction in his very own statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's not a question for him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In addition to Shala, in 1998 you were in Drenica and Prekaz in 1998 with the KLA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 22nd of January, 1998, when the house of Shaban Murat Jashari was attacked by the Serbian police and army in the night, I went on the following day in the morning, at 9.00, to Skenderaj by bus. And from there, I went on foot to visit the family of Shaban Murat Jashari. And it is not true that I went with soldiers but I went by myself with a camera and a video camera and a pencil in my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As for this visit to Murat Jashari, I'm not asking you about that. I'm saying that in Drenica, in Prekaz, you made a propaganda film, and you are featuring in that film, together with KLA terrorists.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not true, and this is very erroneous information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Are you aware of the liquidation of two brothers called Mitrovic, in the village of Mihalici in 1998 also?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the village is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mihalic is the village, the two Mitrovic brothers.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Mihalic is of the Vushtrri commune and never, either before or during or after the war, have I been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mitrovica [as interpreted] and Vucitrn are very close by, as you well know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He says he's not been.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's never been to Vucitrn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was not related to Vushtrri but the question was related to the village of Mihalic. Vushtrri in itself is Vushtrri and the village of Mihalic is Mihalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In May 1999, the KLA in Prilvzje killed six young Serb men below Cicevica. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't remember because I have no knowledge of such a case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know about the village of Sllatine? It is between Vucitrn and Mitrovica. Halfway between the two. Have you heard of that village?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the name of the village and the neighbourhoods they are a part of?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Sllatine, halfway between Vucitrn and Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the first time that I hear of such a village, and I'm sure that there is no such village -- a village with such name in the municipality of Mitrovica or Vucitrn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was burnt down and the population are dispersed. Did you -- have you heard about Nova Selo Macunsko and Banjska? Have you heard of those villages?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I repeat once again: Can you mention the villages with the name that they actually hold? Because I have not heard of such names that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You've never heard of the village of Banjska? Have you heard about Strahini Span [phoen] and the village of Banjska near Kosovska Mitrovica? There are two villages of Banjska but one is close to Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the Banjska village, I know about but previously there was a name which was quite different and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about Novo Selo? Have you heard of that? All right. You've heard of Banjska. You've heard of Macunsko and Novo Selo. Do you know that both those two Serb villages were burnt, like the one a moment ago you said you hadn't heard of?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also know about the village of Magjunaj, formerly Novo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and you don't know about Banjska?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that earlier. I also know about Banjska, and I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that both of them were burnt and who burnt them? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether they are burned, they were burned, and who burned them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you know they were Serb villages, don't you?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that in the village of Magjunaj, there were Serbs and Albanians. It was not an ethnically pure Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The majority of the population were Serbs. In 1998, do you know --

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In 1998, do you know about the killing of two young men in the village of Bukos? Have you heard of the village of Bukos?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard about the village of Bukos, but I have not heard about the killing of two young men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just talking about the killings in Mitrovica. I'm not mentioning any other villages outside your area. Do you happen to know when an incident occurred in the village of Pantina? You've heard of Pantina, haven't you, when a whole family was kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where the Pantina village is, but the village of Pantina belongs to the municipality of Vushtrri, and about this case, it's the first time I hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's very close by, on the edge there. All right. Do you know about Kosovska Mitrovica, on the 13th of January 1999, when an Albanian Nexhmedin Salihu was killed?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about such case, or maybe the name is not said correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Nexhmedin Salihu, an Albanian killed in Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about a certain Nexhmedin who was killed, but I don't know his surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: His surname is Salihu, and he was also killed by the KLA. What about in the village of Supkovac on the 27th of January, when Dejan Kostic was killed? Do you know about that incident?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About this occasion, I have a report about the killing of Dejan Kostic, but as to who killed him, that remained enigmatic and he was found in the street by police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know about the killing, once again in Mitrovica, on the 3rd of February, 1999, when Emir Rexhepi was killed, Emir Rexhepi?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this case or the name may not be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Emir Rexhepi.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BARANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
